name: בֵּית אֵל
summary: Bethel is the town west of Ai, formerly Luz, with Abram’s campsite between the two. Jacob named it after he called the place “the house of God”: בֵּית, construct of בַּיִת “house”, and אֵל “God”.

evidence.note: Abram travels as far as Bethel and returns to the place where his tent had stood between Bethel and Ai.
Abram pitches his tent with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east.
Jacob calls the place בֵּית אֱלֹהִים, “house of God,” and names it בֵּית אֵל. The narrator gives Luz as the town’s former name.

note: Moved from the former word entry `bbeeyt-2eel` (old root key ביתאל, the whole name’s consonants). Its first element is the construct of בַּיִת; the second is אֵל, a word of 2lh.
